s1.syndrome_frame: Subcutaneous swellings with progressive enlargement over months, firm to hard, without pain, and with normal overlying skin
salient_findings: Multiple subcutaneous swellings in the neck, back, and abdominal wall
Swellings are nontender, mobile, and firm to hard
Cytology shows plump spindle cells with abundant eosinophilic cytoplasm and bipolar cytoplasmic extensions
key_facts: 15-year-old girl presented with multiple swellings
Swellings have been progressively enlarging over five months
No significant past medical, personal, or family history
Seven subcutaneous swellings were found on examination
Swellings measure 1×1 to 3×3 cm in size
Complete blood count, metabolic panel, and skeletal survey were all normal
FNAC was performed on the most prominent swellings
Cytology smears showed moderate cellularity with similar features
Spindle cells had round-to-oval nuclei with fine granular chromatin
No nuclear hyperchromasia, pleomorphism, or atypicality was seen
Ultrasonography confirmed lesions were confined to subcutaneous tissue
No lymphadenopathy or deeper masses were found

shortlist.label: Desmoid tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Matches clinical presentation of firm, painless subcutaneous swellings with progressive enlargement

shortlist.label: Fibromatosis
shortlist.why_kept: Similar to desmoid tumor, fibromatosis presents with firm, subcutaneous masses that can grow over time

shortlist.label: Nodular fasciitis
shortlist.why_kept: Presents as a rapidly growing, firm subcutaneous mass, which aligns with the patient's symptoms

shortlist.label: Fibrous hamartoma of infancy
shortlist.why_kept: Although less common in teenagers, this condition can present with subcutaneous masses, making it a plausible differential

shortlist.label: Dermatofibroma
shortlist.why_kept: Common benign skin tumor that can present as a firm, subcutaneous nodule, consistent with the patient's findings

raw.rationale: The clinical presentation of multiple subcutaneous swellings with progressive enlargement, along with the cytological features of spindle cells with abundant eosinophilic cytoplasm and bipolar cytoplasmic extensions, is consistent with fibromatosis. The lack of nuclear hyperchromasia, pleomorphism, or atypicality and the absence of lymphadenopathy or deeper masses also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Desmoid tumor
rejected.why: While desmoid tumors can present as subcutaneous masses, they are typically solitary and can have a more aggressive course, which does not match the multiple, slowly enlarging masses in this case.

rejected.label: Nodular fasciitis
rejected.why: Nodular fasciitis typically presents as a solitary, rapidly growing mass, which contrasts with the multiple, slowly enlarging masses in this case.

rejected.label: Fibrous hamartoma of infancy
rejected.why: Fibrous hamartoma of infancy is a rare tumor that typically presents in infancy, which does not match the age of the patient in this case.

rejected.label: Dermatofibroma
rejected.why: Dermatofibroma is a benign skin tumor that typically presents as a solitary, firm nodule, which does not match the multiple subcutaneous swellings in this case.
